3 · Runtime topology — Client → Gateway → services → private DBs · Eureka discovery · Kafka
Eureka bus — every service registers on boot & discovers the others by name
Config bus — every service pulls its config from config-server on bootstrap
4 · Request trace — "place an order" (numbered badges ①…⑨ map onto Region 3)

g.text: Client sends POST /orders over HTTPS to the API Gateway.
Gateway resolves ORDER-SERVICE via Eureka, load-balances, forwards the REST call.
OrderService validates input, saves Order(status=CREATED) to orders-db.
Calls PaymentClient.charge() (Feign) → payment-service authorizes & writes payments-db.
On payment success OrderService updates Order(status=PAID) in orders-db.
OrderService publishes OrderEvent to Kafka topic "order-events" (fire-and-forget).
notification-service @KafkaListener consumes it, saves Notification, sends email/SMS.
Gateway returns 201 Created + Order JSON to the Client (steps 7–8 happen asynchronously).

svg.text: • Steps 3–6 are synchronous inside one HTTP request; the
• If step 4 (reserve) or step 5 (charge) fails, OrderService
marks Order CANCELLED and releases reserved stock
• Each service owns its own database; no service reads
• Kafka decouples notification: an outage there never
blocks order placement; events are replayed on restart.
• Feign calls resolve logical names through Eureka and are
load-balanced across instances by Spring Cloud LB.
• Cross-cutting config (ports, datasource URLs) comes from
config-server at bootstrap; identity via api-gateway.
Single self-contained SVG · viewBox 3400×2600 · colour-coded per service across folder tree, class diagram and topology · standard UML notation.
